rows.performance_measure_name: % total debt to Council debt limit
rows.story_behind_the_number: Our total debt limit to Council debt limit is forecast at 43 per cent for 2026. The change in the 2026 fiscal year forecast of the Debt Limit between Q2 and Q3 is attributed to a modestly lower revenue forecast, offset by a reduction in forecast borrowing for water utilities projects and fleet acquisitions.

rows.performance_measure_name: City of Calgary credit rating (Standard & Poor's 'S&P rating')
rows.story_behind_the_number: The City of Calgary has maintained high credit ratings over the last 20+ years High ratings show our commitment to long-term financial sustainability.

rows.performance_measure_name: Financial stability ratio (fiscal stability reserve %)
rows.story_behind_the_number: In Q3, our financial stability ratio was 9.0 per cent, which is within The City's target range of 5 to 15 per cent. This ratio measures the balance of our Financial Reserve relative to operating, tax-supported gross expenses (net of recoveries), helping ensure we have sufficient reserves to manage financial risks and unexpected costs.

rows.performance_measure_name: Business license applications that have been submitted and completed online - Ease of Service (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: The metric remains stable at 66 per cent, consistent with previous reporting periods. While no significant increase was observed this quarter, efforts to promote online submissions continue.

rows.performance_measure_name: 311 Telephone Service Factor (% of calls answered in 60 seconds or less)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Typically summer is highest peak call volume for 311. Reduced service levels are expected in Q3 as demand exceeds resources to answer.

rows.performance_measure_name: Trust in The City of Calgary (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Fifty-six per cent of Calgarians say that they trust The City, statistically higher than in fall 2025 (47 per cent) and fall 2024 (41 per cent). This is the highest level of trust since fall 2018.

rows.performance_measure_name: % of Calgarians satisfied with overall City services
rows.story_behind_the_number: In fall 2026, 73 per cent of Calgarians are satisfied with the overall level and quality of City services and programs. This is statistically higher than fall 2025 (67 per cent) and fall 2024 (63 per cent) and marks the second consecutive year of improvement and the highest level of satisfaction since fall 2019.

rows.performance_measure_name: Facility Management Assets in Poor & Very Poor Condition (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Over the last few years, we’ve managed to sustain this indicator below the target through strategic investments, interventions, and preventative maintenance activities. However, this indicator remains highly variable due to ongoing data refinement and buildings that are returned to The City, usually in poor condition. Aging infrastructure and deferred maintenance can also contribute to an increase in this performance indicator. Without sufficient investment and early intervention, these assets are at a higher risk of failure, which may impact the services being delivered out of these buildings.

rows.performance_measure_name: Paved roadways in Good & Very Good Condition (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Additional one-time capital funding in 2026 is helping to slow pavement degradation. Funding is directed at reducing the backlog of very poor and poor roads. The funding level required to achieve the Council-approved pavement quality level of service was presented in the 10-Year Capital Infrastructure Plan.

rows.performance_measure_name: Cumulative lane-kilometres of road repaved
rows.story_behind_the_number: The Pavement Rehabilitation program is 84 per cent complete. Major projects now complete include Macleod Tr., Anderson Rd., 32 Ave. N.E., Shaganappi Tr. N.W., and Builders Rd. & Manhattan Rd. S.E.

rows.performance_measure_name: Sidewalks in Good & Very Good Condition (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Council approved the Concrete Quality level of service that achieves 54 per cent of sidewalks in good condition, zero per cent in poor condition, and reduces safety hazard locations by 72 per cent on September 22, 2026.

rows.performance_measure_name: Pathways in Good & Very Good Condition (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Inspections undertaken in Q2 2026 revealed that the proportion of assets rated Good/Very Good declined year-over-year from 87 per cent to 81 per cent of the total network. This decrease indicates that approximately 84 km of assets shifted from requiring no repairs to standard repair needs, based on pathway inspection criteria. Poor and failing assets remain below 1 per cent of the total network.

rows.performance_measure_name: Park Assets in Poor & Very Poor Condition (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: From 2023–2026, Parks & Open Spaces directed capital funding toward maintaining and replacing aging park assets. This investment helped meet the 2026 target of keeping assets in Poor and Very Poor condition below 22 per cent, achieving a rate of 18 per cent. Continued investment is needed, as many assets currently in Fair condition are expected to decline over the next five to ten years.

rows.performance_measure_name: Cumulative number of repaired potholes (Year-to-Date)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Continuing the trend from Q2 2026, maintenance crews have completed more year-to-date pothole repairs than in 2025 due to additional pothole crews being added to night shift operations and additional contractor support.

These efforts are helping to improve service outcomes: between Q1 and Q3, the number of properties affected by water outages decreased from 8 to 7 per 1,000 properties.

rows.performance_measure_name: Initial 9-1-1 calls answered within 15 seconds (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Typically Q3 is the busiest quarter of the year and performance usually dips below 95 per cent. The result in Q3 2026 is 2.6 per cent higher than the same quarter the previous year, and the rolling four-quarter average for this measure is 94.8 per cent.

rows.performance_measure_name: % of responses to serious and escalating fires (where two engines, one aerial unit, and a minimum of 12 fire fighters arrived) within 11 minutes (cumulative)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Serious and escalating fires were reached within 11 minutes 75.1 per cent of the time, an improvement over last year. Aerial staffing and peak-period coverage engines helped strengthen response performance as population growth and densification continued to increase service demand.

rows.performance_measure_name: Number of responses to encampment sites
rows.story_behind_the_number: There were 1,660 responses to encampments in Q3 and the cumulative total of responses to encampments in 2026 is 4,167. The total number of calls can be made up of multiple calls for the same location, reports of materials left at abandoned encampments, or reports of active encampments.

rows.performance_measure_name: Number of applications processed for the Fair Entry program
rows.story_behind_the_number: The number of applications processed in Q3 2026 declined by four per cent compared to Q3 2025. While demand has stabilized since surging in 2023-2024, the complexity of clients’ needs and ongoing accessibility improvements continue to drive the program.

rows.performance_measure_name: Total number of transit trips (Calgary Transit ridership) (millions)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Bus boardings decreased in Q3 2026 to 23 million from 23.8 million in Q3 2025. This may be in part due to immigration policy changes which have reduced temporary foreign workers and international students- two groups linked to strong transit use. Many other municipalities in Canada are seeing similar ridership trends.

rows.performance_measure_name: Trips that arrive within a specified period (%) (i.e. bus on-time performance)
rows.story_behind_the_number: On-time performance dipped slightly to 84 per cent in Q3 (remaining relatively consistent with 84 per cent Q3 2025 and 84 per cent Q2 2026).

rows.performance_measure_name: Customer safety rating rate on Transit (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Feelings of safety on Calgary Transit remained consistent at 75 per cent in Q3 (vs. 74 per cent in each of Q1 and Q2 2026). Transit Public Safety continued a pilot deploying Peace Officers to targeted CTrain stations.

rows.performance_measure_name: Number of new market homes with development permit approval
rows.story_behind_the_number: There were 4,293 market homes approved through development permits in Q3, representing a 39 per cent increase from the previous quarter and a 25 per cent decline year over year. The decline in year over year development permit is consistent with the softer housing market conditions seen in the first half of the year, driven by weaker demand, rising vacancy rates, growing inventories, and broader economic uncertainty.

rows.performance_measure_name: Number of new market homes with building permit approval
rows.story_behind_the_number: There were 5,260 market homes approved through building permits in Q3, representing an 18% decrease from the previous quarter and a 9% decrease year over year. Though these decreases are observed, the year-to-date trend for building permit approval remains strong. This indicates projects are continuing to advance into the construction phase ensuring that Calgary is restoring pre-pandemic affordability levels.

rows.performance_measure_name: Number of new non-market homes with development permit approval
rows.story_behind_the_number:
There were 169 non-market homes approved through development permits in Q3, representing a 52 per cent increase from Q2 and a 131 per cent year over year increase. 
Growth in non-market housing development is encouraging. Given the funding commitments for new non-market housing projects, more affordable homes will be added to the development and construction pipeline in the next few quarters.

rows.performance_measure_name: Number of new non-market homes with building permit approval
rows.story_behind_the_number: There were 776 non-market homes approved through building permits in Q3, representing more than 8-fold increase from the previous quarter and year over year. These high numbers reflect important progress for projects that were approved following the City’s investment and the Council’s approval of Home is Here Strategy in 2023. Once completed, these homes will be home to 2,000 low-income Calgarians.

rows.performance_measure_name: Total new housing units granted occupancy
rows.story_behind_the_number:
In Q3, there were 6,520 homes completed and ready for occupancy and it was 9 per cent higher than in the last quarter. Completions were at par with Q3 2025. This reflects record housing starts in the last years.
Year to date, multi-residential homes and townhomes have increased as a share of total housing stock, while semi-detached housing, secondary suites, and detached housing declined on a proportional basis.

rows.performance_measure_name: New housing units completed in Calgary's Downtown through the conversion of office properties
rows.story_behind_the_number: Since Calgary's Downtown Office Conversion Program launched in 2021, 793 homes have been delivered through approved conversion projects, including 170 non-market units. Office conversions create more housing choice for Calgarians and advance the Greater Downtown Plan by increasing downtown activity, supporting local businesses and helping create a more vibrant, mixed-use downtown.
